instructions: Pat the steak dry and put it on a plate. Squeeze the juice of 2 limes over it, then add the salt, pepper, oregano and cumin and turn the steak to coat it. Let it sit for 10 minutes while you do the next steps.
Finely chop the onion. Chop about 1/2 cup of cilantro. Cut the last lime into wedges. Put the onion, cilantro, lime wedges and salsa in separate small bowls.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over high heat until it shimmers.

Add half the steak in a single layer and cook for 2 minutes, until the underside is deep brown. Flip it and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until browned on the other side. You're cooking it to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into a thick piece: it's done when there's no red left. Transfer it to a cutting board.
Add the remaining tbsp of oil and cook the rest of the steak the same way.
Chop all the steak into small bite-size pieces. Transfer it to a bowl.
Warm the tortillas one at a time in a dry skillet over medium-high heat for 30 seconds on each side. Stack them in a clean towel to keep them warm.
Taste a piece of the chopped steak. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of lime.
Serve the steak with the warm tortillas, the onion, the cilantro, the lime wedges and the salsa.
method_notes: Honest time is 30 minutes, with a 10-minute lime marinade done while the toppings are prepped. The lead marinates 30 to 60 minutes; I shortened it to fit the night, which gives a lighter lime flavor. Maricruz Avalos stews the chopped steak in water for 15 minutes, a different style, so I kept the lead's quick sear. Both ratings are visible page ratings, not JSON-LD; the Maricruz page had no rating count.
